media:group.media:title: 2026 Revelle Medalist: Joan Heller Brown
media:group.media:description:
A version of this video with audio description track is available here: https://youtu.be/IkxqFijtiT8
The Revelle Medal is the highest honor given by the chancellor of UC San Diego to a retired or emeriti faculty member.
Distinguished Professor Emeritus and Chair Emeritus of Pharmacology Joan Heller Brown is internationally recognized for pioneering research exploring how G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) regulate cell growth, survival and inflammation in heart disease and cancer.
Heller Brown earned her Bachelor of Arts in neurobiology and behavior from Cornell University and doctorate in pharmacology from Albert Einstein College of Medicine. She joined UC San Diego’s faculty in 1975 and was promoted through the faculty ranks over the years. She was appointed chair of the Department of Pharmacology in 2002. During her 17-year tenure as chair, the department experienced substantial growth in faculty and research funding, earning continuous rankings as one of the top pharmacology departments in the nation.
Heller Brown is the principal investigator and director of a National Institutes of Health T32 training grant in cellular and molecular pharmacology, one of the nation’s oldest and largest training grants in pharmacological sciences. She is a fellow of the American Society for Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics and recipient of a Distinguished Scientist Award from the American Heart Association.

media:group.media:title: 2026 Revelle Medalist: Ray F. Weiss
media:group.media:description:
A version of this video with audio description track is available here: https://youtu.be/8Etl8Of6bls
The Revelle Medal is the highest honor given by the chancellor of UC San Diego to a retired or emeriti faculty member.
Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Geochemistry Ray Weiss’ research career began in chemical oceanography and later shifted toward atmospheric chemistry. His oceanographic contributions include quantifying many gas solubilities in seawater, using dissolved atmospheric chlorofluorocarbons as time-dependent oceanographic tracers, and geochemical characterizations of deep-sea hydrothermal vents. In atmospheric chemistry, Weiss carried out the first quantification of the global increase and distribution of nitrous oxide, an important ozone-depleting substance and greenhouse gas.
He co-leads the Advanced Global Atmospheric Gases Experiment (AGAGE), a 13-nation collaboration to measure and model a wide range of trace gases emitted into the atmosphere. AGAGE has made significant discoveries vital to the protection of the ozone layer and the climate.
Weiss has mentored graduate students and postdoctoral scholars who now research and teach geochemistry around the globe. He is a recipient of the Harold Urey Medal of the European Association of Geochemistry and is a fellow of four national and international professional societies.

media:group.media:title: 2026 Revelle Medalist: Frank E. Talke
media:group.media:description:
A version of this video with audio description track is available here: https://youtu.be/nA8XPuczRNU
The Revelle Medal is the highest honor given by the chancellor of UC San Diego to a retired or emeriti faculty member.
Distinguished Professor Emeritus, Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering Frank Talke joined UC San Diego in 1986 after 17 years at IBM. As one of four inaugural chairs of the Center for Magnetic Recording Research, now Center for Memory and Recording Research (CMRR), he helped make CMRR a leading university-industry research center. As chair, Talke guided the growth of the Department of Applied Mechanics and Engineering Sciences, helping shape today’s Departments of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Bioengineering, Structural Engineering, and Chemical and Nano Engineering.
His 390 publications and 11 patents span information storage technology, drop-on-demand inkjet printing and engineering in medicine, including computer-navigated spinal procedures using MRI and augmented reality. Since retiring in 2022, Talke has continued mentoring graduate and undergraduate students whose work took first place in UC-wide and Jacobs School of Engineering competitions.
Talke is an Honorary Member of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) and a member of the National Academy of Engineering.

media:group.media:title: 2026 Revelle Medalist: Paul A. Insel
media:group.media:description:
A version of this video with audio description track is available here: https://youtu.be/xPX_OB4XIJg
The Revelle Medal is the highest honor given by the chancellor of UC San Diego to a retired or emeriti faculty member.
Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Pharmacology and Medicine Paul A. Insel is a physician-scientist whose research advanced understanding of how cells receive and respond to signals in the body. His work on G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) explored their expression, signaling, regulation and roles in health and disease. He has published more than 300 original research articles and 190 other publications and holds multiple patents.
Insel earned his medical degree from the University of Michigan and completed training in internal medicine at the Harvard Medical Service at Boston City Hospital, followed by research training at the National Institutes of Health and UC San Francisco. He joined the UC San Diego faculty in 1978.
A leader in physician-scientist education, Insel served as director and co-director of the School of Medicine’s Medical Scientist (MD-PhD) Training Program from 1989 to 2025. He has received numerous honors, including the Bert Shapiro Award from the National Association of Clinician Scientist Training, for which he served as founding president.

media:group.media:title: 2026 Revelle Medalist: Judith A. Dolan
media:group.media:description:
A version of this video with audio description track is available here: https://youtu.be/9oW0sA-pEko
The Revelle Medal is the highest honor given by the chancellor of UC San Diego to a retired or emeriti faculty member.
Distinguished Professor Emerita of Theatre and Dance Judith A. Dolan is a Tony Award-winning costume designer whose five-decade career spans more than 120 theatre and opera productions and 11 film and television projects. Her work has appeared on stages around the world, from Broadway in New York City to the Abbey Theatre in Dublin.
Dolan joined UC San Diego in 1998 after earning a doctorate in drama from Stanford University. She is perhaps best known for her longtime collaboration with Broadway director and producer Harold Prince, including the revival of “Candide,” which earned her a Tony Award for Best Costume Design. At UC San Diego, Dolan mentored generations of theatre artists and held numerous leadership roles, including associate dean of the School of Arts and Humanities and head of design. Her career has been honored by the League of Professional Women. Her professional service includes membership on the Tony Award Nominating Committee and executive board of the National Design Portfolio Review.

entry.title: Taking the Bite Out of Mosquito-Borne Disease

media:group.media:title: Taking the Bite Out of Mosquito-Borne Disease
media:group.media:description:
Mosquitoes are the deadliest animals on Earth, but new science could change that. At UC San Diego, researchers are engineering mosquitoes to help bring us closer to a world free from mosquito-borne diseases like malaria and dengue.
This work represents a new approach to prevention, protecting people, reducing strain on health systems and moving us toward a future where mosquito-borne disease no longer threatens lives.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at: @aking-the-bite-out-of-mosquito-borne-disease/

entry.title: The Right Cancer Care, Right Now

media:group.media:title: The Right Cancer Care, Right Now
media:group.media:description:
What if cancer patients didn’t have to wait weeks for answers? At UC San Diego, researchers are developing AI-powered tools that rapidly analyze biopsies — helping doctors identify the best treatment options faster, more accurately and at lower cost.
By reducing delays between diagnosis and care, these tools have the potential to save lives, ease uncertainty for patients and expand access to precision cancer treatment.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at: @he-right-cancer-care-right-now/

entry.title: Revolutionizing Preventative Healthcare With Just A Touch

media:group.media:title: Revolutionizing Preventative Healthcare With Just A Touch
media:group.media:description:
UC San Diego engineers and medical researchers are creating wearable sensors that continuously track health markers like blood pressure, glucose, fatigue and hydration. These sensors turn everyday movement into actionable data, helping doctors detect issues earlier and deliver more personalized care.
By monitoring multiple biomarkers at once, this technology makes it easier to manage medical conditions and optimize health seamlessly and in real time.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at: @evolutionizing-preventative-healthcare-with-just-a-touch/

entry.title: The Best Lab is Real Life

media:group.media:title: The Best Lab is Real Life
media:group.media:description:
The Living Lab brings UC San Diego researchers and older adults together to explore what supports strength, independence and connection as people age. From fall prevention to brain health, residents help turn research into practical tools that enhance everyday care.
By meeting people where they are, the Living Lab lowers barriers to participation and transforms aging research into solutions that improve lives today and for generations to come.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at: @he-best-lab-is-real-life/

entry.title: Harnessing the Power of Human Milk

media:group.media:title: Harnessing the Power of Human Milk
media:group.media:description:
Human milk is universal, and its health benefits extend far beyond infancy. At UC San Diego’s Human Milk Institute, researchers are uncovering how human milk supports immune health, development and healing across the lifespan.
As the world’s first research institute dedicated solely to human milk, HMI brings together scientists, clinicians, engineers and community partners to turn discovery into better care and equitable access. From infant health to chronic disease research, this work is expanding what’s possible and who benefits.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at: @arnessing-the-power-of-human-milk/
